title: Visual Gaze Stabilization
opening: Before editing one paragraph, you notice yourself checking several other windows. Choose whether to rest your gaze on the page, remove the interruptions, or skip the option.

labels.figure: A seated reader working at a notebook at a desk
labels.rested: Rest your gaze briefly on the page. Inbox, calendar, and chat remain open.
labels.closed: Close the unnecessary windows. The reading page stays visible.
labels.unchanged: Leave the scene as it is. The gaze option is optional.
labels.practice: Record a real comparison if useful

practice.prediction: What task are you preparing for, and what do you expect the gaze option to change? Keep the expected task result separate from the action.
practice.observation: If you try it in a safe, stationary setting, what did you actually do? If you did not try it, record that instead.
practice.comparison: Record the surrounding conditions that matter, including other visible or audible interruptions and whether you changed them. For a useful comparison, say what stayed the same.
practice.result: What happened in the actual task? Record the work or result you can inspect separately from how focused you felt.
practice.revision: Did the option feel comfortable and change a useful transition? If it caused discomfort or added no useful change, omit it. What would you revise?
practice.step: Choose a next comparison, or leave this optional. What would you check in a later representative task? Name one setting where narrow gaze would be unsafe.

feedback.unavailable: Saving is unavailable for this lesson. Your notes remain on screen.
feedback.missing: Complete all six reflection fields before saving, or keep the notes on screen.
feedback.readFailure: Your saved notes could not be loaded. Your current notes remain here.
feedback.conflict: These notes changed elsewhere. Your answers remain here. Save again to keep these answers.
feedback.readbackFailure: The save could not be confirmed. Retry to check the same save.
feedback.saveFailure: The save is uncertain. Retry to check the same save.
feedback.retryPending: The earlier save is still unresolved. Retry the same answers before changing them.

source.status: The reader, page, and competing windows are an authored illustration. The manuscript supplies no measured gaze or learner outcome. A subjective sense of focus is not sufficient evidence of cognitive enhancement. Removing unnecessary windows may address the interference directly.
